reviews.review: needs better direction for its progression
ArcRunner is something i can see myself playing a lot more of. the maps are great.

Graphics are gorgeous and gameplay is very enjoyable, although not all weapons are useful. Music is repetitive but very good and I don't really get tired of it though I'm certain you can turn it off if desired. I bought the game planning to play on easy but as I'd initially feared rewards are reduced if you don't play on normal so I reluctantly tried it. It's hard at first until you get some practice and unlocks but this game gets easier over time even more than upgrading stats would suggest at first glance. I'd say its a great balance which is hard enough to feel rewarding but easy enough to still beat. The only other game I felt that way about is Dragon's Dogma. I recently beat the second stage boss and unlocked the powerful hacker class which I'm really loving. This game is extremely addictive as long as you like its style and I highly recommend it.

This game is amazing. I haven't really ever felt the need to take the time to post a review, but after seeing how few people have tried this game out and how great it is, I figured posting a review would help persuade people to give it a try. I am so glad I did.

This game is like a cross between Borderlands, Warframe,  and Mortal Shell's DLC.

The gunplay mechanics are great. Lots of variety in the types of guns and checking every drop for the perfect blend of stats and mods on the weapons reminds me a lot of the looting aspects of Borderlands.

Fighting against hordes of enemies and using the perfect combination of weapons, abilities, and melee is what will help you survive. That gameplay style reminds me a lot of one of my favorite games of all time, Warframe.

Finally, going the distance in a single run and building up your nanites resource to continuously buff your stats that carry over from run to run for that great roguelite experience. Punishing, yet forgiving at the same time that is very rewarding when you get further and further each run. It provides that nerve wracking suspense that potential death provides while rewarding your for making it as far as you did so that next run you can go even further. I loved Mortal Shell's DLC and this game is very similar to those roguelite mechanics.

This game is absolutely worth the price of admission and the developer is very active to make sure they continue to provide updates. I highly recommend you give it a try.

Like a game from an alternate 1980's where they had the tech. Challenging, beautiful, and clever. Could use a little polish, but I'm impressed at their updates and responsiveness so far. Easily worth the price if this is your kind of thing.

A lot of fun to play, i don't know why people are comparing this to risk of rain so much as it is NOT like risk or rain other than that it is a roguelike game. Its progression and game play are most similar to Gunfire Reborn. If you like gunfire reborn or other looter shooter roguelikes and the cyberpunk aesthetics you will likely enjoy this game.

The only thing I can say as a negative is that there are currently only 3 classes and the only unlockable one (the hacker) feels significantly more powerful than the other 2 alternatives. However this seems to be an intended result as you have to get relatively far before unlocking this class and this class is intended to make the journey back easier.

[b]ArcRunner,[/b] a third person roguelite shooter game with cyberpunk theme. A game where you fight against robots that went rampant, just like in many kinds of sci-fi settings. Of course, you’re handed with guns and a melee weapon of your choice.

You’ll start with initially [b]two classes[/b] in the game, a Soldier where you can use a shield that deflects back shots to your enemies, or a Ninja where you can hide using your stealth kit, and attack them where they least expect you. There’s another class, Hacker. However, you’ll get said class near the end of the game.

[b]The gameplay is as simple[/b] as a third person shooter will be. You shoot, you get items if there’s anything interesting, then you’ll get to another area. You’ll get upgrades through the level that increases your stats, rinse, and repeat. If you die, you’ll get permanent upgrades later so you’ll have an easier time on the later run. Plus, you’ll unlock weapons if you get at least around 100-250 kills with said weapon, depending on which you are using..

This game borrows some mechanics from other games, where [b]every weapon has its own rarity.[/b] Simply put, said weapons have their own modifier, whether they can ricochet, deal damage over time or maybe increase some of the stats. It does give a bit of weapon variety, which is something I do like.

As for the graphics and such, It’s normal. Nothing much to say here, but the 2D hand-drawn character designs look cool. I suppose I should give some credits to the art designer.

[b]Coop is working fine and well.[/b] Played with some randoms and it does work fine! In fact, this is one of the reasons why this game won’t be boring. But, since this is a peer-to-peer co-op, if the host got disconnected, everyone else will.

While the game is quite okay, there are some problems that I had with the game, whether it’s the feel of the gameplay or progression-wise. There are some problems that I had with the UI and some others, so…

[b]Here are the problems I mentioned.[/b]

[b]The progression is quite grindy for a small unlock.[/b] The only thing you’ll unlock is something +xx% more damage, more this and that or just unlock a basic thing like secondary weapons and an ultimate.

[b]The ultimate skill for the Ninja class isn’t appealing.[/b] Probably make it fast or make it quite flashy a little bit?

[b]The game feels boring early on.[/b] There are barely any good things that make the game unique compared to other games, which I understand why people can be turned off at first glance. What I’m saying is the game is quite shallow in terms of mechanics. Some reviews on Steam already pointed out this. 

[b]The game really drags on[/b] when it comes to advancing to new areas. Not to mention, since the areas look quite the same on all 7 levels, it doesn’t really help either. My suggestion is to make a sub-area inside said areas, maybe 3-3-1 sub areas, where the first one is quite… peaceful(?), then the second one has some ruins or some signs of changes around said area, then finally, the boss. Or just make it condensed, take Binding of Isaac as an example.

[b]The effects are either unfitting or it doesn’t exist.[/b] Makes the game feel… off? As if I’m not hitting anything? Or when I do, it feels wrong. There’s way less kick on the shots, melee feels like I’m slicing or slamming the air, and so on. This also applies to the effects into the game where you melee attack things, which leads to FPS drop.

[b]Oh, the UI. Ugh.[/b] I’ll give you a video of it.
https://youtu.be/zHdGArimXfM
Simply put, the nanite requirement for upgrades are barely readable, sometimes I get confused since it blends so hard to the icon and the background. Simple fix would be changing the nanites needed (the text!) to green, which is one of the color palettes they barely use. This is a really simple fix.

On the good side…
[b]Only one unintended camping area for challenges[/b], no bugs and glitches so far.
Here's the said area:
https://youtu.be/EZ0fZPQgJWw

I’ll give this game… [b]B- out of S, a mixed review, leaning a bit into positives. Just a bit.[/b] ArcRunner is a basic third person shooter roguelite game, with cyberpunk style. It does have its base mechanics doing alright, however the game is quite shallow which leads to the game not engaging at times, especially in early games. I suggest buying this game on sale. However if things got changed the right way, I might be able to recommend this game fully.

9/10. Arcrunner is what we get if doom and returnal had a beautiful baby.

It keeps returnal's roguelike elements and third-person perspective (can switch left, right or center with a button), lets go of the downtime and replaces it with doom's "combat chess" wave-based arena fights against enemies who have specific roles/archetypes akin to chess pieces. (no disrespect to returnal. it's absolutely a roguevania masterpiece, but sometimes it takes long periods between fights due to the exploration elements of metroidvanias. which is fine because it's just returnal being itself, a roguevania. thankfully, its tower dlc gives what the doom players want: ultra nightmare (permadeath) runs. which is exactly what we have in arcrunner, a roguelike ultra nightmare run.)

Combat-wise, I like that there are so many ways to defend against enemy attacks. You can sprint, dash, quickstep, strafe, jump, double jump, hover, shield, stealth cloak, deflect, redirect, decoy, counter shoot and more, using the gadgets and augments. And the ways to attack are just as many. Spray with the smg, run and gun with the shotgun, stand back and snipe with sniper rifle, go all rounder with an assault rifle, be a gunslinger with the magnum revolver, there's a blade disc thrower that's basically a crossbow with ricocheting bolts, take down multiple enemies in a single shot with a freakin sci-fi bow and arrow, fry groups of enemies with the chain lightning gun (essentially a flamethrower) or in contrast smash frozen enemies with the cold gun and melee attack, or just straight up delete enemies with the supershotgun. With all the different weapon mods, things get even wilder. There are more heavier weapons I haven't mentioned so maybe check this game out.

The loot pool is small but everything has purpose and function. Builds do not rely on loot but rather on the arcrunner augments system. (players saying there's not enough loot for different builds are looking at the wrong place! xD) These augments are key to success the same way properly built god boons in hades are.

Combat is tough but fair. All enemy attacks, including the bosses, have a tell you can react to and defend properly. There are always indicators where the enemies are and when/where enemies are spawning. There's no excuse. If you lose, it's on you. You won't ever lose because of sheer amounts of overwhelming hostiles. You have to know your enemies' roles, be methodical and in complete control of your arcrunner to win.

I also like that, as I said earlier, there's little to no downtime. All the exposition you need are at the boot/intro cinematics and the very first conversation which are all skippable (as well as the rest of the cutscenes/dialogues). It's almost non-stop action aside from the optional looting in between arena fights. When it's game over, you can go straight back in (from the beginning xD).

I have minor nitpicks but I'm not gonna mention those because nitpicks are not criticisms.

All that being said, along with the great artstyle, music and everything down to the co-op mode, arcrunner is everything I want in a game and I wish there were more games like these. Great job, devs! ;)

I know roguelike purists don't like roguelites. I agree to an extent but my simple solution to that is: to play roguelites as roguelikes, by not using the meta-progression. Give it a try. :)

also, this game getting not recommended reviews because it's not like risk of rain 2 or gunfire reborn is ridiculous.:/ it's apples and oranges. RoR2 is a roguelike horde survival like vampire survivors. gunfire reborn is a standard roguelike fps, but it seems very corridor shooter-ey(?) despite being proc-gen'ed. both are very different from arcrunner which is more like its parents, doom and returnal.
